Incidental finding deferred from TKT-126's second ai-review pass ([PR #116](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/116)). Pre-existing at `origin/main`; TKT-126 preserved the behaviour deliberately rather than expanding scope, and recorded the asymmetry in ADR-033. Likely a slice of TKT-127.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — re-verified against HEAD `ac2952b`

**Still real.** `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:201` still dispatches on `knownSchemas[msg.Subject()]` with no `env.Type` check; access checks it in both consumers (`consumer.go:360`, `policy.go:96`). Note the ticket suggests folding this into TKT-127 — TKT-127 is now **Done**, so this is standalone.

**Verdict: still worth doing → Ready.** Not DoR-baked: the 8-item shaping happens when the ticket is claimed, per the owner's drain-the-debt call.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Merged into TKT-123 — do not claim

This ticket's scope now lives in **TKT-123** (Shared durable-consumer contract checks: distinguish durable deletion, validate envelope type against subject), which carries it verbatim under an *Absorbed TKT-133* section. Moved out of Ready so it cannot be picked up in parallel. Nothing was dropped — reopen this only if the merge is reversed at plan time.

description:
### Finding (TKT-126 ai-review, second pass, 2026-07-27)

Inventory's catalog consumer **never validates the envelope's `type` field**. It dispatches purely
on the NATS subject (`knownSchemas[msg.Subject()]`, `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go`)
and ignores `type` entirely. Access's two consumers both check it
(`env.Type != SubjectOrderCompleted`, `env.Type != SubjectPerformancePublished`).

**This is pre-existing** — it is true at `origin/main` before TKT-126, whose decode types carried no
`type` field for inventory at all. TKT-126 left the behaviour unchanged by design (its whole safety
property was disposition parity), and recorded the asymmetry in ADR-033 rather than silently fixing it.

### Why it matters

An event published on `platform.catalog.performance.published` carrying
`"type":"platform.catalog.performance.archived"` — or no `type` at all — is provisioned and acked.
ADR-009 §5 makes `type == subject` part of the envelope contract, so inventory currently accepts
envelopes that violate it.

There is also an inconsistency TKT-126 introduced, deliberately and with a test
(`TestDecodeEnvelopeRejectsNonStringType`): a **non-string** `type` now fails the shared decode and
terminates, while a **wrong-string** `type` is still accepted. Inventory's disposition therefore
depends on the JSON representation of the same contract violation.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Inventory validates `env.Type` against `msg.Subject()` before schema dispatch, or the decision
      not to is recorded with a reason (dispatching on the subject may be the deliberate design —
      the broker, not the payload, is the routing authority).
- [ ] Whatever is decided, missing / mismatched / non-string `type` reach the **same** disposition
      class rather than three different ones.
- [ ] Consumer-level tests pin the chosen behaviour for all three shapes, at a known and a future
      schema, asserting the exact action sequence and the readiness outcome.
- [ ] ADR-033's "what deliberately does not live here" section and the `domainevent` package doc are
      updated to match whatever is decided.

### Notes

Consider doing this **inside TKT-127** (the shared durable-consumer skeleton), which is where the
`id`/`type` checks are already flagged as belonging — this may be a slice of that rather than a
standalone change.
